PanelText: David was the youngest son of Jesse, a shepherd boy who watched his father's sheep in the hills near Bethlehem. One day his father sent him to the army camp with bread and cheese for his older brothers, who were soldiers in King Saul's army.

PanelText: Every morning and evening, a giant warrior named Goliath stepped out from the Philistine army and shouted his challenge: “Send me a man to fight me! If he beats me, we will be your servants — but if I beat him, you will serve us!” For forty days, no one dared to answer him.

PanelText: David heard the giant's taunts and said, “Let no one lose heart — I will go and fight him.” King Saul offered David his own armor, but it was too big and heavy for a shepherd boy. So David laid it aside, took his shepherd's staff, and chose five smooth stones from the stream.

StoryDescription: A shepherd boy, a giant warrior, and a God who wins the battle — the story of David and Goliath from 1 Samuel 17, told panel by panel.
PanelImageCredit: Art coming soon — Lorraine's own artwork will appear here.
PanelText: David ran toward the battle line, slipped a stone into his sling, and swung it around his head. The stone flew straight and struck Goliath on the forehead. The mighty giant crashed to the ground, face first, before the eyes of both armies.

StoryDescription: A shepherd boy, a giant warrior, and a God who wins the battle — the story of David and Goliath from 1 Samuel 17, told panel by panel.
PanelImageCredit: Art coming soon — Lorraine's own artwork will appear here.
PanelText: David had won — not with a sword or heavy armor, but with a sling, five stones, and trust in God. “The battle is the Lord's,” he had said, and all Israel saw that God saves His people. When giants stand in your way, remember: the God who stood with David stands with you.
